statement: Kernel-checked adaptive final theorem: if 0<theta<1 satisfies PI(theta), then every fixed 0<c<(1-theta)/3 gives the stated prime divisor for all sufficiently large k and 2k<n<=exp(c(log k)^2/loglog k). The older balanced 9/23 endpoint is an artifact. For the explicitly named location-blind, termwise-nonnegative certificate class, Lean additionally proves the exact block invariant (2r-1)log(T1)+(r-1)log(T2)=log(delta)+4log(W), its W>=1 monotonicity and finite safe-tail budget, and the leading LP equivalence LocationBlindTermwiseLeadingCertificate(theta,c) iff c<(1-theta)/3 for c>0. Thus c>=(1-theta)/3 is kernel-refuted in that leading parameter class, including c>=19/120 at theta=21/40. The bridge from every growing subdivision to the LP image remains a natural proof; Erdős 451 itself is not closed.

dependency_gaps: The abstract theta theorem assumes PI(theta); the theta=21/40 corollary imports the Baker--Harman--Pintz short-prime input exactly as the source paper does.

The complete adaptive four-range theorem is kernel-checked. For the enlarged no-go, the exact block algebra and leading LP frontier are kernel-checked, but the PI cardinality-tail reduction and weighted extraction of a good block from an arbitrary growing subdivision remain natural-proof steps rather than a formalized sequence-of-partitions theorem.

The no-go is confined to the named location-blind deterministic-tail class whose nonnegative Theorem 4.1 bounds are summed and required to be o(k^theta/log k). It does not cover sparse covers selected from actual prime locations, cross-block cancellation, stronger prime inputs, stronger exponential-sum estimates, or the true bad-set cardinality.
Novelty and publication priority remain unchecked.
